intro_html: Kibbeh is the national dish of Lebanon and it comes in a dozen forms. The tray version, kibbeh bil sanieh, is the one built for feeding a crowd: a bulgur and meat shell on the bottom, a spiced meat filling in the middle, another shell on top, scored into diamonds before it bakes. Warm allspice runs through the whole thing. Each serving carries 41 grams of protein and 576 calories for about $4.15 (at everyday cost), and it cuts into portions like it was designed for meal prep, because in a sense it was.
cost_closing_html: About $4.15 a serving (at everyday cost). Five pounds of turkey is the cost of this dish; the bulgur, onions, and spices together come to very little. Bulgur is one of the most underused cheap grains in an American grocery store.
shop_smart: Bulgur is sold cheapest in international grocery stores and in the bulk aisle, often at half the price of the small boxes in the rice section. Fine grind is what you want for the shell layers.
Onions are doing enormous work here at seven of them. Buy them by the bag rather than loose, since bagged onions run well under the each price.
Allspice is the defining spice and a single jar lasts for years. If you buy one new spice for this recipe, that is the one.
Fresh basil stands in for the traditional mint here. If your store carries fresh mint at a similar price, use it instead, and dried mint works too.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cover the bulgur with cold water and let it soak 20 to 30 minutes until the grains soften, then drain it and squeeze out every bit of excess water with your hands.
Set aside about a third of the ground turkey and a third of the onions for the filling, then finely mince the remaining onions for the shell.

Mix the soaked bulgur with two thirds of the ground turkey, the minced onion, the ground allspice, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper, kneading it with wet hands until it turns into a smooth, almost paste-like dough.

For the filling, heat some of the olive oil in a skillet and brown the reserved turkey with the reserved diced onion, seasoning it with more allspice, salt, and black pepper, then stir in the chopped fresh basil off the heat.
Press half the bulgur mixture into an oiled 9x13 pan in an even layer, spread the filling over it, then press the remaining bulgur mixture on top, smoothing it with wet hands.
Score the top into diamonds with a wet knife, cutting through the top layer only, then drizzle the rest of the olive oil generously over the whole surface.
Bake at 375F for 40 to 45 minutes until the top is deep golden and the edges pull away from the pan, then rest 15 minutes before portioning.
portion_html: Weigh the pan, subtract the empty pan weight, and divide by 14. The scored diamonds give you a natural cutting guide, but weigh them anyway since the corner pieces always run small. Each serving comes to 576 calories and 41 grams of protein.
upsell_html: A Lebanese classic built for a crowd, about $4.15 a serving (at everyday cost). This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, for $1 a month.

steps: Soak the bulgur in cold water 20 to 30 minutes, then drain and squeeze it dry.
Knead the soaked bulgur with two thirds of the ground turkey, minced onion, allspice, cumin, salt, and pepper into a smooth dough.
Brown the remaining turkey with diced onion and more allspice for the filling, then stir in the chopped basil.
Press half the bulgur dough into an oiled 9x13 pan, spread the filling over it, and press the rest of the dough on top.
Score the top into diamonds, drizzle with olive oil, bake at 375F for 40 to 45 minutes, rest 15 minutes, and portion into 14 containers.
